You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    c.id,
    c.series_name,
    c.Country,
    c.Language
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ca
    ON ca.Channel = c.id;
```
Gotta find out which countries these tv channels are from.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    c.Country
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ca
    ON ca.Channel = c.id
WHERE c.Country IS NOT NULL;
```
I need to check if these tv channels are actually showing the cartoons.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    c.id AS channel_id,
    c.series_name AS channel_name,
    c.Country,
    ca.Title AS cartoon_title,
    ca.Original_air_date
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ca
    ON ca.Channel = c.id
WHERE ca.Title IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY c.Country, c.series_name, ca.Title;
```
I need to check if the cartoons are written by Todd Casey.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    c.id AS channel_id,
    c.series_name AS channel_name,
    c.Country,
    ca.Title AS cartoon_title,
    ca.Written_by,
    ca.Original_air_date
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ca
    ON ca.Channel = c.id
WHERE ca.Written_by LIKE '%Todd Casey%'
ORDER BY c.series_name, ca.Title;
```
